$comment: The reading list. Edit this file, then run `pnpm reading-list` to regenerate docs/reading-list.md and docs/reading-list.html. Each link has a title, a url, one or more topics, an optional system, and an optional note.

groups.name: Accessibility standards
groups.intro: Each design system's own accessibility pages are under Accessibility in the design systems section.

groups.name: Design systems, by topic
groups.intro: The same links as the by-system section, grouped so each topic can be compared across systems. A system missing from a topic has no page for it.

groups.name: Components, by type
groups.intro: Each system's page for the same kind of component. The names differ: Atlassian's "toggle" is a switch, and Carbon's "content switcher" is a segmented control.

topics.name: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide
topics.intro: How each kind of component should work with a keyboard and screen reader. Read the matching pattern before building a component.

links.title: Refactoring UI: Building your color palette
links.note: The most practical short read. Grays, primary, and accent colors, and how to build 9 to 10 shades of each.

links.title: Stripe: Designing accessible color systems
links.note: Why HSL lightness doesn't match how bright a color looks, and how Stripe rebuilt its palette so every hue has the same contrast at each step.

links.title: Matt Strom: How to generate color palettes for design systems
links.note: Perceptual color spaces, shifting hue as colors get lighter or darker, and generating scales from formulas.

links.title: Radix Colors: Composing a palette
links.note: Choosing a brand color, a gray tinted toward it, and status colors.

links.title: Radix Colors: Understanding the scale
links.note: What each of 12 shades is for: backgrounds, borders, fills, and text.

links.title: OneSignal: 11 shades of gray
links.note: A case study of building a gray scale.

links.title: The 60-30-10 rule for UI design
links.note: A rough guide to how much of a screen is neutral, supporting color, and accent.

links.title: Shopify: How to choose brand colors
links.note: A general branding guide.

links.title: Adobe: Picking your brand colors
links.note: Another general guide, in three steps.

links.title: Color psychology: how colors influence the mind
links.note: A skeptical, research-based take. Fit with the brand's personality and standing out matter more than what a hue "means."

links.title: Labrecque and Milne, "Exciting red and competent blue"
links.note: Research on how hue, saturation, and lightness shift a brand's perceived personality.

links.title: Singh, "Impact of color on marketing"
links.note: The source of the often-quoted "up to 90% of snap judgments" figure. Widely repeated, loosely sourced.

links.title: WCAG 2.2
links.note: The full standard.

links.title: WCAG 2.2 quick reference
links.note: The easier way in: every criterion, filterable, with techniques.

links.title: Understanding WCAG: Target size (minimum)
links.note: Where the 24px minimum comes from.

links.title: Designing for macOS
links.note: Where the 28pt Mac target size comes from.

links.title: Toggles
links.note: Switches, plus checkboxes and radio buttons in its macOS section.

links.title: Offering help
links.note: Help tags; there's no tooltip page.

links.title: Window size classes
links.note: Material's breakpoints.

links.title: Button groups
links.note: The newer connected button group.

links.title: Text fields
links.note: Multi-line text is part of text fields; there's no separate text area.

links.title: Button (Forge UI Kit)
links.note: Default, primary, subtle, warning, and danger.

links.title: Button usage
links.note: Emphasis levels, one primary per page, and danger buttons.

links.title: Text input
links.note: Text areas are a section of this page.

links.title: Button (Android)
links.note: How one system sizes a control per platform.

links.title: Segmented control (iOS)
links.note: IOS only; the web has none.

links.title: Polaris web components
links.note: The newer version.

links.title: Checkbox (web components)
links.note: The React page now redirects here.

links.title: Button group
links.note: Its segmented variant.

links.title: Text field
links.note: For a text area, use its multiline option.

links.title: Question pages
links.note: Where "mark optional fields, no asterisks" comes from.

links.title: Focus states
links.note: The yellow focus style.

links.title: Button accessibility tests
links.note: An example of publishing how each component was tested.

links.title: Button group
links.note: Its segmented variant.

links.title: Text input
links.note: Text areas are a section of this page.

links.title: Outline
links.note: The 4px focus outline.

links.title: Spinner accessibility
links.note: No built-in announcement: the page adds its own live region.

links.title: Loading
links.note: Which loading indicator for how long a wait: nothing under one second.

links.title: Spinner source
links.note: Sizes, role, and delay, which the usage page doesn't list.

links.title: Progress (material-web)
links.note: The web component's sizes and labelling.

links.title: Divider (SwiftUI)
links.note: No options: it runs across a stack, so it turns vertical inside a row.

links.title: Divider (material-web)
links.note: Inset variants; decorative unless you add role="separator".

links.title: ActionList dividers
links.note: Primer has no standalone divider; ActionList's is hidden from screen readers.

links.title: Menu sections with separators
links.note: No standalone divider: a menu Section's hasSeparator draws a border.

links.title: Divider
links.note: Vertical, four strengths, inset, and words in the middle. No built-in margin; hide a purely visual one with aria-hidden.

links.title: Divider (web components)
links.note: Whitespace often groups better than lines, and too many add clutter.

links.title: Section break
links.note: An <hr> whose margin is the point; the line is optional.

links.title: WAI-ARIA 1.2: the separator role
links.note: A separator that can't be focused is a static structural element; its children are presentational, so words inside it aren't read.

links.title: Should an hr be read by screen readers? (freee)
links.note: Announce it by default; if you'd want it skipped, ask whether the line is needed at all.
